record.paper_title: Ordered Banach algebras and multi-norms: some open problems
record.original_question: For a locally compact group G and p in [1, infinity), the source notes that M(G) has an isometric Banach-lattice-and-algebra isomorphism into L^r(L^p(G)) when p=1 or G is amenable, and it asks whether amenability of G is actually necessary for the representation of M(G) in L^r(L^p(G)) to be a lattice homomorphism when p>1. It also asks whether the left regular representation of M(G) in L^r(M(G)) has analogous Banach-lattice-and-algebra properties.

evidence.quote: It also follows from [ 2 , 3 ] that there is an isometric Banach lattice and algebra isomorphism of M ( G ) into \({\mathcal L}^r\big (L^p(G)\big )\) for any \(p\in [1,\infty )\) if either \(p=1\) or G is amenable. It does not seem to be so clear that the left regular representation of M ( G ) in \({\mathcal L}^r\big (M(G)\big )\) possesses these properties.
Update: In view of [ 11 ], is the amenability of G necessary for the representation of M ( G ) in \({\mathcal L}^r\big (L^p(G)\big )\) to be a lattice homomorphism in the case \(p>1\) ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a locally compact group and let $M(G)$ denote its measure algebra, equipped with its standard Banach-lattice structure (variation norm and ordering by signed/complex measures) and convolution product. For $p\in[1,\infty)$, write $\mathcal{L}^r(L^p(G))$ for the Banach lattice of regular operators on the complex Banach lattice $L^p(G)$, endowed with the regular norm and with composition as its algebra product. For $\mu\in M(G)$, the convolution operator $T_\mu:f\mapsto \mu*f$ on $L^p(G)$ is regular, and the assignment $\Phi_p:\mu\mapsto T_\mu$ is a contractive algebra homomorphism $M(G)\to\mathcal{L}^r(L^p(G))$. It is known that $\Phi_p$ is an isometric Banach-lattice-and-algebra isomorphism (in particular a lattice homomorphism) whenever $p=1$ or $G$ is amenable.

(a) For $p\in(1,\infty)$, is amenability of $G$ a necessary condition for $\Phi_p:M(G)\to\mathcal{L}^r(L^p(G))$ to be a lattice homomorphism?

(b) Does the left regular representation $\Psi:M(G)\to\mathcal{L}^r(M(G))$ defined by $\Psi(\mu)(\nu)=\mu*\nu$ yield an isometric Banach-lattice-and-algebra isomorphism of $M(G)$ into $\mathcal{L}^r(M(G))$?

The status appears unknown from available public sources.
